resources.string: Reads the 6-digit pairing code from the system \"Pair device with pairing code\" dialog, only within 10 minutes after you tap Start pairing, so you do not have to type it. It never reads other screens and never stores or uploads anything.
Notifications are off: the pairing-code box cannot appear in the shade (tap to fix)
Add this app to the battery whitelist
On your computer run: adb connect %1$s\nIt recovers by itself after a reboot, a Wi-Fi reconnect or sleep.%2$s
\nAuto-read pairing code: on (no need to copy the 6 digits next time)

ADB works right now, but it will not come back after a reboot (usually after uninstall + reinstall).\nFix: turn on Wireless debugging, then tap the button below — the app re-grants itself.\nOr re-run omniadb setup on the computer / run pm grant over USB.
Repair scheduled; if Wireless debugging is on, the permission will be granted automatically
Permission ready — pairing is all that is left
Tap \"Start pairing\" below, then go to Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code.%1$s
\nThe code is read automatically, so you do not have to copy it.
\nThe code appears in the notification shade; type it there.

One pairing is enough to obtain the permission; after that no computer is needed.\nTap \"Start pairing\" → Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code, then type the 6 digits in the notification shade.
Auto-read pairing code: written to settings but not bound (tap the button below)
Auto-read pairing code: off (tap the button below to turn it on)

1. Tap the button below; the app reads the code by itself\n2. Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code\n3. When the 6 digits appear you can ignore them, the app submits them

1. Tap the button below; the app puts an input box in the shade
2. Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code
3. Pull down the shade, type the 6 digits and submit
 (the pairing screen stays open, it will not be closed)
[Fallback] Enter the pairing code and port manually
Enter the pairing code and port first
Once paired, this phone brings ADB back to port 5555 by itself after a reboot, a Wi-Fi reconnect or sleep.\nOn the computer just run: adb connect <phone IP>:5555
Input box placed in the notification shade. Next, open the Wireless debugging page to pair
Without notification permission the pairing box cannot appear in the shade. Notification settings opened.
No permission to write system settings, switching to manual. If the switch is greyed out: App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings
Sent, waiting for the system to bind…
Settings written, but the system has not bound the service yet. Check the switch in Accessibility; if it is greyed out: App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings
Add this app manually: Settings → Battery → Unrestricted
Open Settings → Developer options → Wireless debugging
Open Settings → Apps → OmniADB Host → Notifications
Tap \"Enable keep-alive\" in the app to resume
Turn on Wireless debugging and finish the one-time pairing in the app
Finish the one-time pairing in the app (pairing also grants the permission and pins the port)
Missing WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS (self-granting needs Wireless debugging to be on). Turn it on and tap \"Check and repair now\", or run: adb shell pm grant %1$s android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
Wi-Fi did not come up; retrying automatically later
Looking for the Wireless debugging port
Switch command sent, but port %1$d is still unreachable
%1$s\n(No WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS: it will not recover after a reboot. Run: adb shell pm grant %2$s android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS)
Self-granting through the local ADB connection
Establishing trust with the local adbd
Establishing trust with the local adbd (port %1$d)
Pairing failed. Check that the code and port are correct and that the dialog stayed open
Getting the permission and switching to the fixed port…
Shows the state of the ADB keep-alive service
Waiting for pairing: turn on Wireless debugging and pair
Running %1$s (no permission, will not auto-recover after a reboot)
Type the pairing code in the notification shade during one-time pairing
OmniADB: enter the wireless debugging pairing code
Looking for the pairing port… open \"Pair device with pairing code\" in Wireless debugging
Pairing port %1$d found. Pull down this notification and enter the 6-digit code
Go to Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code, then pull down this notification and enter the code
Pairing port not found. Keep the \"Pair device with pairing code\" screen open
Pairing failed. Check the pairing code
The pairing server closed. Reopen the pairing screen
